### **Job Description and Duties**


Do you aspire to work towards protecting our population and the environment from harmful chemicals? Then consider joining the Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC), Safer Consumer Products (SCP) Program. Our team is a dynamic, passionate, and diverse group of scientists, engineers, toxicologists, analysts, and administrative staff working to protect California's people and the environment by advancing the design, development, and use of chemically safer products. SCP is seeking an Environmental Scientist to help implement laws banning certain chemicals in consumer products, including developing regulations and conducting compliance and enforcement activities. This position is under the general direction of a Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory). Learn more by visiting our homepage at https://www.dtsc.ca.gov/SCP/.  

**As an Environmental Scientist you will have the opportunity to:**
* Conduct technical research and data analysis to support the development of regulations, compliance sampling plans, and enforcement strategies, including identifying manufacturers and evaluating covered products to understand the scope of regulated products sold in California
* Assist with drafting rulemaking packages and preparing documentation to implement statutory and regulatory requirements in compliance with the Administrative Procedures Act
* Assist with pre\-regulatory workshops, public meetings, and external engagement activities, including outreach to manufacturers, retailers, and other interested parties
* Support the procurement and cataloging of samples for laboratory testing to carry out compliance sampling plans
* Analyze testing results and review documents submitted by responsible entities to assess compliance with chemical bans
* Provide technical assistance and compliance support to responsible entities, including manufacturers and retailers
* Help prepare public\-facing resources such as guidance documents, fact sheets, and website content to keep interested parties informed of compliance requirements and enforcement actions
* Assist with compliance and enforcement activities, including conducting investigations, preparing notices of violation, and developing documentation to support enforcement actions
* Draft reports to inform the Legislature, the public, department leadership, and agency management of compliance and enforcement updates

**Desirable Qualifications We Look For:**
* Ability to contribute to a team environment that values the diverse areas of experience and expertise of program staff
* Technical/Environmental Health writing \& editing experience
* Ability to identify a challenging problem and formulate and execute a solution
* Can complete long\-term projects
* Has ability to analyze and work with large volumes of data and information
* Ability to focus on maintaining professional, productive relationships with their peers, management, and external partners
* Knowledge of or experience with products, chemicals in products, or supply chains
* Strong communication skills, including editing, writing, and presenting
* Ability to maintain a well\-organized and flexible approach appropriate for working in a dynamic environment

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Job Description and Duties**


This position supports the California Department of Public Health’s (CDPH) mission and strategic plan to advance the health and well\-being of California’s diverse people and communities by becoming a learning, healing, and impactful organization.  

The Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) (SESS) supports national, state, and local environmental health emergency preparedness programs as a liaison representing the Center for Environmental Health (CEH). The SESS collaborates with decision makers across governmental and private sectors, professional, and community\-based organizations, including tribal organizations, to develop policies, procedures, plans and training for environmental health emergency preparedness, response, and recovery. The SESS leads multijurisdictional initiatives to integrate statewide emergency support functions related to environmental health, and builds cross\-sector partnerships to enhance coordination, with a focus on advancing health equity.  

  

The SESS works under the direction of the Environmental Program Manager I (EPM I) of the Training and Partnership Section (TPS) in the CEH.

**Telework Information**

This position may be eligible for telework. The amount of telework permitted is at the discretion of the Department and is subject to change, consistent with CDPH’s Telework Program. All employees who telework are required to be California residents in accordance with Government Code 14200\. Candidates who reside outside of the state of California may be interviewed; however, the selected candidate must have a primary residency in the state of California prior to appointment (and continue to maintain California residency) as a condition of employment. Failure to meet this requirement may result in the job offer being rescinded.  

Travel may be required for this position. Reimbursement for travel takes into consideration an employee’s designated headquarters, as reflected in the duty statement, and is subject to regulations and bargaining unit contract provisions. All commute expenses to the designated headquarters office will be the responsibility of the selected candidate.  

The headquarters office location for this position is identified in the attached duty statement.

### **Department Information**


At the California Department of Public Health (CDPH), equity, diversity, and inclusion are at the core of our mission to advance the health and well\-being of California’s diverse people and communities. We are genuinely and strongly committed to cultivating and preserving a culture of inclusion and connectedness where we can grow and learn together with a diverse team of employees. In recruiting team members, we welcome the unique contributions that you can make to us and the work we do.


The Center for Environmental Health (CEH) is home to inspection, technical assistance, regulatory, investigation, and emergency response activities that ensure compliance with regulations and improve the safety of foods, industrial hemp products, drugs, and medical devices to protect and improve the health of all Californians. CEH conducts age\-related and flavor ban tobacco enforcement, regulates radiation machines/producers and radioactive materials, ensures proper disposition of low\-level radioactive waste, regulates the generation, handling, and disposal of medical waste; and conducts other environmental management programs. The CEH includes the Division of Food and Drug Safety, the Division of Radiation Safety and Environmental Management and the Training and Partnership Section (TPS), which focuses on emergency preparedness and One Health.


The TPS partners with local, state, and national entities to prevent and mitigate environmental public health risks and strengthen resiliency through program support to adapt and scale up in the face of emerging needs and priorities using a One Health approach.
